svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
The projection plane
Visibility as versioned snapshots — written with the commit, consumed at leisure, never the truth. Lag here is a quality problem, not a correctness failure.
THE SOURCE
THE WORKERS
THE INDEX + READS
The row rides the commit
Every committed transition inserts one projection row inside
the same fenced transaction as history and timers. There is
no separate publish to lose.
projection_log — PK (partition, fanout, run_key, seq)
payload: one full VisibilitySnapshot per transition
The snapshot contract
A complete post-transition image — status, lifecycle, times,
lineage, full memo and search-attribute images — tagged with
archetype_id · authority_epoch · source_transition_seq
Applying a later version never depends on having seen an
earlier one: retries and out-of-order delivery are harmless.
Archetype-neutral — workflows and CHASM components share it.
ProjectionWorker — one per partition
batch 256 · run_from_cursor(checkpoint)
Reads the log in order, hands snapshots to the sink, saves its
checkpoint on an interval — and never advances past a sink
error. Restart resumes from the stored cursor; replay is the
same read, again.
projection_checkpoint — keyed by partition
property-tested: no advance on failure
The monotonic sink
Upsert-iff-newer on (authority_epoch, source_transition_seq):
the newest snapshot replaces the visible generation; stale or
repeated deliveries change nothing. Idempotent by contract.
search-attribute images land as one generation
VisibilityRepairScanner — CHASM-side
Rebuilds a component's snapshot from its persisted root node and
re-applies it, version-keyed: a still-projected execution is a no-op,
a dropped one is repaired. Workflow rows ride the commit — they
cannot go missing in the first place.
One shared index, two generations
execution_visibility_current · _attr_index · _rollup
The archetype-aware generation: typed attribute index with
generations, rollups striped 16 ways by run key.
vis_execution · vis_rollup — the legacy pair, still present
Both live in DSQL beside the authoritative tables — visibility
is SQL, not a second datastore.
9-table sa_* search-attribute index family
VisibilityQueryService
List, count, and describe surfaces — the Temporal visibility
grammar answered from the index. Reads never touch the
commit path.
The plane's one rule:
history is the record and the snapshot is a copy — every component here may lag, fail, or replay freely, because none of them can change what happened.
Flow annotations

g.text: The snapshot is derived from committed state at commit time — its contents and the history it summarizes cannot disagree, by construction.
Workers consume the log asynchronously, one per partition, in order — a worker that dies resumes from its checkpoint and re-reads the same rows.
The sink writes into the shared index; upsert-iff-newer makes every delivery safe to repeat and every ordering safe to receive.
Queries answer from the index alone. A lagging projection returns slightly old truth — never wrong truth, and never blocks a commit.
Key: clay = rides the fenced commit · dashed slate-blue = derived consumption · teal = reads · dashed grey = repair
Until chasm-foundation Stage 1, this plane spoke a delta contract (ProjectionOp). Snapshots replaced it: self-sufficient rows beat replayed folds.
